description: MSC 1's actual WebSocket surface, per docs/msc2/rolling-plan.md P0.24 (amended). MSC 1 has exactly one real-time WebSocket channel, not the six msc2-engineering.md §5 describes for MSC 2's intended design (D-006) — see the Amendments log in rolling-plan.md.

channels.name: console

requiredHeaders.Connection: must contain 'upgrade' (case-insensitive substring match, not exact)

handshake.successResponse: HTTP/1.1 101 Switching Protocols, with Upgrade: websocket, Connection: Upgrade, Sec-WebSocket-Accept: <computed>
handshake.failureResponse: HTTP 400 {"error": "websocket_upgrade_failed"} if Sec-WebSocket-Key is missing or empty

auth.mechanism: Identical Bearer-token check applied to every HTTP route, evaluated before the WS-upgrade special case is reached
auth.requiredRole: any authenticated role (admin, guest, or named) may connect — GET requests carry no additional per-path permission gate
auth.failureStatus: 401 Unauthorized for a missing/invalid token (or 429 Too Many Requests if the per-IP auth-failure rate limit has already tripped, per RemoteAPIAuthFailRateLimiterTests)

payload.framing: one JSON-encoded ConsoleLineDTO per WebSocket text frame (opcode 0x1, FIN bit set)

deliveryModel.backfillSource: tailConsoleLines(n: 200), sent as 200 individual frames immediately on successful upgrade, before any live line
deliveryModel.liveSource: every new console line appended to consoleBuffer is broadcast to all currently-connected WS clients as it arrives
deliveryModel.ringBufferBehavior: consoleBuffer (backing both this backfill and GET /console/tail) is capped at 5000 lines (consoleBufferLimit); oldest lines are trimmed via removeFirst(overflow) once the cap is exceeded

inboundHandling.textFrames: intentionally ignored — the server never executes WebSocket-received text as a command; POST /command is the only command-execution path (RemoteAPIWebSocketTests.testWebSocketUpgradeAndInboundTextIgnored pins this)
inboundHandling.pingFrames: opcode 0x9 -> server replies with a pong frame (opcode 0x8A) carrying the same payload
inboundHandling.closeFrames: opcode 0x8 -> server replies with a close frame (opcode 0x88, empty payload) and tears down the connection
inboundHandling.fragmentation: not supported — MSC 1 does not reassemble frames with FIN=0; source comment reads 'Ignoring fragmentation for now'

frameSizeCap.onExceeded: server sends a close frame and tears down the connection

channels.notes: status, operation-progress, players, notifications, and metrics are NOT WebSocket channels in MSC 1 — they're HTTP-polled (GET /status, GET /players, etc.), not pushed. There is no 'channel' concept anywhere in RemoteAPIServer+WebSocket.swift; every JSON-send call site sends a ConsoleLineDTO specifically. The 'six channels' language in msc2-engineering.md §5 describes MSC 2's intended design, not MSC 1's actual baseline — per D-006 this file captures MSC 1 as it is; those five would-be channels are Phase 2 design work, not something to invent here.
